newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products weaker, except naphtha, gasoline.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products weaker, except naphtha, gasoline.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mostly weaker with crude on Wednesday, but naphtha and gasoline held up on tight supply, traders said.
Gasoline supply was increasingly short, especially for high octane grades, pushing prices up to parity with northern Europe.
Good demand was reported for both Turkey and Lebanon, and superplus cargoes were talked around Rotterdam premium unleaded barges +$30 cif Lavera.
A Romanian cargo was reportedly sold to a U.S. tanking company, although this arbitrage was closed to most traders.
Most shorts in northern Europe were covered for October.
Paraffinic supply was tight as Algeria's Skikda port remained shut for the second night due to bad weather.
Gas oil prices were eroded by futures, but spot premiums for heating oil firmed slightly. Traders said heating oil cargoes were bid at Nov IPE +$7 cif Lavera, about $1 above Tuesday.

Low sulphur diesel premiums were not so strong, with demand in the Med well covered and cargoes going north to take advantage of the high price differential. Egypt tendered to buy up to 150,000 tonnes of 0.5 percent sulphur gas oil for delivery in January to March.
The tender called for three cargoes in Suez and three in Alexandria.
Fuel oil was weaker with crude.
High sulphur cracked cargoes were steady to a touch weaker around $117-118 fob Med as bullish talk about Romanian demand was finding fewer takers.

Low sulphur cracked markets were seen to be a touch easier. A one percent straight-run cargo was offered at $134 cif, at least $4 off yesterday's offer price. An M-40 was heard offered around $135 cif, some way off a bidder at $130.
